flights.title: Outbound: Sofia → Istanbul → Tokyo Haneda
flights.when: Mon 9 Nov 21:40 → Tue 10 Nov 19:45 (15 h 5 min)
legs: Layover 2 h 20 min in Istanbul, change of plane
TK198 Turkish Airlines, Istanbul (IST) 02:30 → Tokyo Haneda (HND) 19:45, Tue 10 Nov
flights.notes: 2 adults. Land 19:45, hotel about 22:00 (APA is informed). Getting to the hotel is decided on arrival.

flights.title: Return: Tokyo Haneda → Istanbul → Sofia
legs: TK8364 (operated by All Nippon Airways), Tokyo Haneda (HND) 08:55 → Istanbul (IST) 16:45
Layover 3 h 45 min in Istanbul, change of plane
flights.notes: Leave Kc-III ~5:30 (taxi ~¥2,500–3,000). ANA-operated, so probably Terminal 2: confirm on ANA Flight Status on Sat 21. Collect the suitcases at the airport by ~6:00 (see Transfers).

stays.title: Tokyo: APA Hotel Asakusa Tawaramachi Ekimae
stays.extra: Rooftop public bath 6:00–10:00 and 15:00–01:00, free. 1 min to Tawaramachi Stn (Ginza Line), 5 min walk to Kappabashi. Free cancellation until 8 Nov 23:59 (Japan time); €257.56 from 9 Nov; €505.01 from 10 Nov. No changes possible.
stays.notes: On arrival ask reception: can they send the suitcases to Kyoto (they only use the post, not Yamato), and phone Tama Sushi for Wed 11.

stays.title: Kyoto: HOTEL TAVINOS Kyoto
stays.checkin: Self check-in machines from 15:00, check-out 11:00. Front door locked 00:00–6:00 (the room key card opens it).
stays.ref: Booking.com 8679902396128212992; check-in number A26103018851 (show with passport)
stays.extra: Kyoto accommodation tax ~¥400 pp per night may be collected at check-in. Free cancellation until 9 Nov 23:59 (Japan time); €279.67 from 10 Nov; €458.48 from 11 Nov. No changes possible. Accepts parcels before arrival (write the date of stay and guest name on the label). Does not send parcels.
stays.notes: The suitcases from Tokyo arrive here on Sat 14 by Japan Post.

stays.title: Yoshino: Chikurinin Gunpoen (竹林院群芳園)
stays.checkin: Check-in 15:00–18:00 (dinner only if checked in by 19:30), check-out 10:00
stays.extra: Japanese-style room (shared toilet), dinner + breakfast, ¥57,540 (~€326). Free shuttle from Yoshino Station at 14:30 (confirmed). Small bags can be left before check-in. Public bath 16:00–22:00 and 6:00–9:00 (most likely heated water, not onsen); private bath ¥3,300 per 50 min (available). Choose the bath slot and the dinner time (from 18:00) at check-in. Free cancellation until 14 Nov 23:59 (Japan time).
stays.notes: Small bags only: the suitcases stay in Kyoto/Osaka (see Transfers). Message 1 was sent on 5 Nov.

stays.title: Osaka: Hanastay Aya (花渓居 绫)
stays.extra: One-bedroom house, 34 m², tatami with 2 futons, kitchen, washing machine, bathtub. €258 (¥45,427 incl. ¥4,000 cleaning fee). 3 min walk to Tamade Stn (Yotsubashi Line). Free cancellation until 17 Nov 23:59 (Japan time); date changes not possible.
stays.notes: Message 2 (suitcases) sent on 5 Nov; waiting for the host's answer. We never wait at the house for a delivery.

stays.title: Haneda: Kc-III (last night)
stays.checkin: Self check-in 16:00–22:00 only (send the arrival time in advance), check-out 10:00. Quiet hours 21:00–8:00.
stays.extra: One-bedroom apartment, 31 m², double bed + sofa bed, bathtub, kitchen, washing machine. €80 / ¥14,040 incl. VAT. 9 min walk to Ōtorii Stn (Keikyū Airport Line, ~7 min to Haneda T1/T2). Free cancellation until 7 Nov 23:59 (Japan time); ¥7,020 from 8 Nov; ¥14,040 from 23 Nov.
stays.notes: Unmanned, so it probably can't receive parcels. Arrival ~17:30 on Sun 22.

transfers.title: Tokyo → Himeji (→ Kyoto)
transfers.how: Shinkansen Nozomi 111, Green Car, car 10, seats 13-C and 13-D (Fuji side). smartEX reservation 2000, ¥45,280 for two. QR ticket on the smartEX site; take the Seat Information slip at the gate. Leave the hotel ~5:20.
transfers.luggage: Suitcases go ahead to HOTEL TAVINOS Kyoto by Japan Post (APA if they can, otherwise Asakusa Post Office on Thu 12 ~17:45; delivery Sat 14). Day bags only.
transfers.notes: Himeji → Kyoto is not booked yet: reserve on smartEX by Fri 13 (tour ends 12:30, Kōko-en after, train about 14:15).

transfers.title: Kyoto → Osaka suitcases
transfers.when: Tue 17 ~9:00 hand-in, collect Thu 19 ~18:30 (or Fri 20 morning)
transfers.how: First option: Yamato hold. Hand in at Yamato Shimogyo Center (Gojo Karasuma; Oe-cho 556, Matsubara, Higashitoin-dori), held at Yamato Namba Station Center (4-4-4 Namba). Collect Thu 19 ~18:30 with passport and tracking number (handover until 20:00 per Yamato's list). Second option, if Yamato refuses: Japan Post Yu-Pack at Yanagibaba-Matsubara Post Office (counter opens 9:00), held at Nishinari Tamade Post Office (Tamade-naka 2-10-17); collect Fri 20 morning.
transfers.luggage: We travel to Yoshino and Nara with small bags only. No waiting at any apartment.
transfers.notes: At the Kyoto counter ask that the Namba office accepts the hold, the price (about ¥4,700 for both) and the exact address line.

transfers.title: Kyoto → Fushimi Inari → Uji → Yoshino
transfers.how: Keihan Kiyomizu-Gojō 5:49 → Fushimi-Inari 5:56; JR Inari 8:33 → Uji 8:50; after the tea ceremony JR Uji 11:52 → Nara 12:21 → Ōji 13:07 → Yoshinoguchi 13:42, Kintetsu Yoshinoguchi 13:48 → Yoshino 14:21. Uji → Yoshino ¥1,630 each. The Wakayama Line showed an operations notice: check on the day. Chikurinin shuttle from Yoshino Station at 14:30.
transfers.notes: Taihō-an tea ceremony is fixed at 11:00 (RSV_261118_16).

transfers.title: Yoshino → Nara → Osaka
transfers.how: Ropeway Yoshinoyama → Senbonguchi (~¥500, cash). Kintetsu Yoshino 10:07 → Kashiharajingu-mae; limited express 11:07 → Yamato-Saidaiji 11:27; Nara Line 11:34 → Kintetsu-Nara 11:40 (¥1,550 each with the limited express). Back: Kintetsu-Nara 17:47 → Osaka-Namba ~18:30 (~¥680). Then Yotsubashi Line Namba → Tamade (¥240) and 3 min walk.
transfers.luggage: Collect the 2 suitcases at Yamato Namba Station Center on arrival (first option).
transfers.notes: Train times are from Jorudan: verify on the day. Regular Kintetsu and JR local trains need no booking (tap Suica).

transfers.title: Osaka → Haneda
transfers.how: Metro Tamade → Daikokuchō → Shin-Osaka (29 min, ¥290). Nozomi 416, car 14, seats 17-D and 17-E (Fuji side), smartEX reservation 2001, ¥29,440 for two. Shinagawa: Keikyū Rapid-Limited Express 17:00 → Keikyū-Kamata 17:06 (¥230), Airport Line to Ōtorii, 9 min walk to Kc-III.
transfers.luggage: Not decided. Option A: Japan Post Airport Yu-Pack from Tamade Post Office on Fri 20 (about ¥6,670 for both), pickup JAL ABC counter, T3 3F. Option B/C: Yamato Airport TA-Q-BIN from Yamato Namba Station Center on Sat 21 (about ¥7,260), pickup T2 3F (5:45–23:00) or T3 2F (6:00–23:00). Overnight bags only from the hand-in.
transfers.notes: Ask at a Japan Post office if the suitcases can wait at the airport until Mon 23. Check the TK8364 terminal on ANA Flight Status on Sat 21.

transfers.title: Kc-III → Haneda airport
transfers.how: Taxi to the terminal, ~¥2,500–3,000 (first train not verified). Terminal 2 expected for TK8364.
transfers.luggage: Collect the suitcases by ~6:00 with the receipt and passport. Free terminal bus T3 → T1 → T2 if needed (first 4:47, every 4 min from 5:00).
transfers.notes: Flight 08:55. The ANA check-in counter opening time is not verified.

phrases.use: To call staff, get past someone, or apologise. The most useful word of the trip.

phrases.jp: ありがとうございます
phrases.use: After any service, a meal or help.

phrases.jp: こんにちは / おはようございます
phrases.use: Entering a shop, a guesthouse or a small restaurant.
After dark, instead of konnichiwa.

phrases.jp: さようなら / では、また
phrases.use: Sayōnara is quite final. Dewa, mata is the everyday one.
Hai also means 'I hear you', not always 'I agree'.
Add it to anything, or just point and say it.
Before a longer question.
Polite and enough on its own.

phrases.jp: もう一度お願いします
phrases.use: When you missed it.

phrases.en: Sorry, I only speak a little Japanese
phrases.jp: 日本語は少しだけです
phrases.use: A good answer after someone starts talking quickly.
At the door of a restaurant. Show two fingers too.
Then give your name.
Some small izakaya still allow smoking.
Ask for an English menu: 'eigo no menyū'.

phrases.jp: 英語のメニューはありますか？
phrases.say: eigo no menyū wa arimasu ka?
phrases.use: Before you try to read the wall.
Said before the first bite, hands together. Ee-TAH-dah-kee-mahss.

phrases.en: Excuse me, we would like to order
phrases.jp: すみません、注文お願いします
phrases.use: How to call staff and order: raise a hand, and say it clearly. Many tables also have a call button.

phrases.jp: 注文してもいいですか？
phrases.say: chūmon shite mo ii desu ka?
phrases.use: When someone is close by and looks free.
Point at the dish or the item.

phrases.jp: これとこれをお願いします
phrases.use: Point on the menu as you say each one.

phrases.jp: これを一つお願いします
phrases.use: Numbers: hitotsu 1, futatsu 2, mittsu 3.

phrases.jp: ビールをお願いします
phrases.use: Any beer.

phrases.jp: 生ビールを二つお願いします
phrases.use: Nama means draft. Hold up two fingers.
The classic izakaya first line: the drink comes while you read the menu.

phrases.jp: おかわりお願いします
phrases.use: A refill of the same drink or rice.
Often free, and sometimes self-service.
Point at the dish.
At a counter or a small place where the chef decides.
At a sushi counter.

phrases.jp: わさび抜きでお願いします
phrases.use: Replace wasabi with any ingredient: "... nuki de".
Drinks.
To the cook, with a nod.
When leaving or paying.

phrases.jp: ラストオーダーは何時ですか？
phrases.say: rasuto ōdā wa nanji desu ka?
phrases.use: Often 30–60 minutes before closing.
Say "sumimasen" first. Many places pay at the register, not at the table: take the slip there.
Markets, small restaurants and temples are often cash only.
When leaving a restaurant.

phrases.en: I have an allergy / I can't eat ...
phrases.use: Show the written word on the phone. Audio example: "I can't eat shrimp."
Markets and shops.
If the staff come to help.
Bags cost a few yen.
Have your passport ready. Minimum ¥5,000 before tax.
Kappabashi knife shops.
Kappabashi. It can take 1–3 days.

phrases.jp: 写真を撮ってもいいですか？
phrases.say: shashin o totte mo ii desu ka?
phrases.use: In shops, on tours and always before photographing a person. Never photograph geiko or maiko without asking.

phrases.jp: 御朱印をお願いします
phrases.use: At the stamp desk (御朱印 / 納経所), after praying. Hand over your book, open.
Anywhere.
Show the name on the phone if the answer is long. Audio example: Kyoto Station.

phrases.jp: この電車は…に行きますか？
phrases.say: kono densha wa ... ni ikimasu ka?
phrases.use: On the platform. Audio example: Nara.

phrases.jp: ここまでお願いします
phrases.use: Taxi: show the address on the phone.
Show the map.

phrases.jp: チェックイン / 荷物を預けたい
phrases.use: At a hotel or a Yamato counter. For takkyūbin held at an office: 営業所止め (eigyōsho-dome).

phrases.en: I would like to send this suitcase
phrases.jp: このスーツケースを送りたいです
phrases.use: At a post office or Yamato counter.

phrases.en: Hold at the Yamato office, please
phrases.jp: 営業所止めでお願いします
phrases.use: Yamato Shimogyo, Tue 17.

phrases.en: Hold at the post office, please
phrases.jp: 局留めでお願いします
phrases.use: Japan Post second option.
Tell staff or anyone close by.
Or ask the hotel reception.
Emergencies.

phrases.jp: 救急車 / 警察を呼んでください
phrases.use: Or dial 119 / 110 yourself.

emergency.what: Bulgarian Embassy out-of-hours emergency (EU consular page; verify before the trip)
Emergency calls are free from any phone. Say 'kyūkyū' (ambulance) or 'jiko / keisatsu' and your address.
Your travel insurance 24 h number: add before departure

packing.item: Passports (valid for the whole trip) and printed or offline copies of the bookings
packing.why: Hotels ask for passports at check-in; phone batteries die.

packing.item: Clean socks without holes
packing.why: Shoes come off at Himeji Castle, temples and the Yoshino lodging.

packing.item: Slip-on, comfortable walking shoes
packing.why: Shoes come off many times a day, and we walk 15,000+ steps on most days.

packing.item: Layers: light fleece or sweater, packable jacket, a scarf
packing.why: Mid-November is 5–17 °C, cold mornings at 6:00–7:00 (Kyoto, Yoshino) and warm midday sun.

packing.item: Compact umbrella or light rain jacket
packing.why: Showers are possible; Takao on Fri 13 is decided by the weather.

packing.item: Cash in yen (a pouch for coins)
packing.why: Markets, Chanko Kawasaki, Kizu Market, ropeway, many temples and small restaurants are cash only.

packing.item: Cards that work abroad, plus an IC card (Suica / ICOCA on the phone)
packing.why: Metro, buses, konbini and most trains: tap.

packing.item: Power bank and short charging cables
packing.why: Maps, tickets and QR codes all live on the phone.

packing.item: Plug adapter type A (Japan is 100 V)
packing.why: Bulgarian plugs do not fit; check chargers for 100–240 V.

packing.item: eSIM or roaming plan
packing.why: Maps, translation, smartEX QR tickets and timetable checks.

packing.item: Small hand towel or handkerchief
packing.why: Many public toilets have no towels or dryers.

packing.item: Tissues and a small bag for rubbish
packing.why: Few public bins; carry rubbish until the hotel or a konbini.

packing.item: Small gifts or a thank-you item (optional)
packing.why: For hosts and guides who helped.

packing.item: Goshuin book (buy at Nezu Shrine on Wed 11)
packing.why: Collecting temple and shrine stamps along the route.

packing.item: Compact day bag or backpack
packing.why: Day bags only on Sat 14 (Himeji), Wed 18–Thu 19 (Yoshino, Nara).

packing.item: Medication and a basic first-aid kit
packing.why: Pharmacies are easy to find, but some medicines common in Europe are restricted: check the Japan rules before you pack them.

packing.item: Laundry sachets or a small detergent
packing.why: Washing machines at Aya and Kc-III.

packing.item: Foldable bag for souvenirs and knife purchases
packing.why: Kappabashi knives go in the checked bags only, never in the cabin.

packing.item: Earplugs and a sleep mask
packing.why: Overnight flight out, thin walls in the Yoshino lodging.

packing.item: Face masks (optional)
packing.why: Many locals wear them in crowded trains.

checklist.task: APA Tokyo: free cancellation ends 8 Nov 23:59 (Japan time). Keep the booking or decide before then.
Kc-III Haneda: free cancellation ends 7 Nov 23:59 (Japan time); ¥7,020 from 8 Nov. Keep it or decide now.
HOTEL TAVINOS Kyoto: free cancellation ends 9 Nov 23:59 (Japan time).
Chikurinin Yoshino: free cancellation ends 14 Nov 23:59; Hanastay Aya ends 17 Nov 23:59.
Passports valid and packed; Visit Japan Web done (immigration and customs QR codes saved).
Online check-in for TK1030 and TK198 (opens 24 h before departure); for TK8364 / TK1029 on Sun 22.
Travel insurance bought; the 24 h number and policy number saved in the Emergency section and on the phone.
eSIM or roaming active; offline maps for Tokyo, Kyoto, Yoshino, Osaka downloaded.
Suica / ICOCA added to the phone wallet and topped up.
Yen cash ordered or planned for the first days; cards checked for foreign use.
smartEX: Nozomi 111 and 416 QR tickets saved offline; Himeji → Kyoto to be reserved by Fri 13.
Reply from Hanastay Aya (suitcases): check and answer. Chikurinin answered (shuttle, bags, bath, dinner).
Kc-III: arrival time (~17:30 on Sun 22) sent.
Luggage: ask APA on arrival; Thu 12 ~17:45 Asakusa Post Office if needed; Tue 17 ~9:00 Yamato Shimogyo Center. Osaka → Haneda option still to decide.
Tue 10 arrival: ask APA reception to phone Tama Sushi (dinner on Wed 11? ~17:30). Backups T24b / T24c.
Book Shinjuku Unatetsu for Fri 13, 16:30, 2 people (Wed 11 or Thu 12; Ikyu, 100% cancellation fee).
Thu 12 evening: decide Takao (Option A) or the rain day (Option B) from the forecast.
Decide and book by Wed 18: Kobe beef (O5a / O5e), fugu lunch (O19), Tsukinone (O25), Kyoto dinners (K11, K15, K16).
Confirm the Osaka Castle volunteer guide (Fri 20 13:00) when the confirmation arrives; agree the meeting point.
Sat 14: check tenryuji.com for the early opening (7:30) on Sun 15.
Sat 21: check the terminal for TK8364 on ANA Flight Status (probably T2).
Wed 18 morning: check the JR Wakayama Line operations notice.
Pack the suitcases (150 cm and 137 cm) and day bags; check the size limits (158 cm on Turkish and ANA).
